title: Great moments of emotional break downs in film.

commenti.body:
Jamie Lee Curtis in the Feast of the Seven Fishes episode of The Bear is the best I have seen. 

Sally Field at the end of Steel Magnolias. 

I think Tom Cruise does a good job in Jerry Maguire right before Cuba Gooding Jr says “you are hanging on by a very thin thread”.
[removed]

On the more realistic side of things the scene of Tom Hanks breaking down at the end of Captain Phillips is one of the best portrayals of shock in film. It's very unexpected at a point in the narrative where audiences would normally expect a release of tension and instead are given completely different type of emotional catharsis. Plus the use of non-actors in the scene gives it an almost surreal feeling of being outside of the normal events of the film.
Oh yes, that's a good one!
[removed]
[removed]
[removed]

Mads Mikelson in Riders of Justice is always the one that comes to my mind. I’ve never seen an actor embody such complex emotions in such a physical manner. Going from rage to incomprehension to sobbing like a baby. It’s such a powerful moment to betray multiple stages of grief in just a minute or so. Not to mention that he literally breaks a mirror with his head, no special effects.

When >!the parents are watching the footage of their kids getting murdered!< in Sympathy for Lady Vengeance. In my opinion, the most difficult-to-watch scene in the director’s filmography, and he already specializes in soul-crushing, and this is in a genre that specializes in soul-crushing.
[removed]
Jamie gave me a heart attack on that one and Sally broke my heart on Steel Magnolia. Such incredible performances.
[removed]
I would have to go with Gil Birmingham in Wind River after his conversation with the FBI agent. The scene to which I refer had me weeping in the theater. It is a truly harrowing watch.

I've always loved the part in Small Apartments where the main character sings He Ain't Heavy, He's My Brother while driving and thinking about memories with his brother.

https://youtu.be/UJ9IfKgu08s?si=eDMmNrC4tIKl5FLR
[removed]

Breaking The Waves (1996 - Lars Von Trier). Bess coming to see Jan off as he gets on the helicopter headed for the oil rig. You can find the clip online but it takes the whole movie to (try to) understand her reaction. Wonderful movie

For me it's Mei finally breaking down and crying in My Neighbor Totoro.

I'm a grown ass man that didn't see this movie in its entirety until I was 30, and her tears just wrecked me. She is so brave, she does such a good job of holding it together. Even when she trips and falls flat on her face, you can see her holding back tears but refusing to let herself lose composure. That scene where she falls is what makes the later breakdown so powerful for me. Once she finally addresses the elephant in the room to talk about her mom, the dam breaks and she starts crying, I start crying. There's catharsis in it.

This movie is extremely precise, and all the emotions of all the characters in it feels real. The daughter, the three friends, even the little fucktoy. It’s one of the best Danish films, and one of Anders Thomas Jensen’s best.

Paul Giamatti in Sideways the moment Miles finds out his ex, Vicky was expecting. You can see the exact moment his already fragile heart completely shatters, realizing she’s gone for good, leading to him bailing entirely on the wedding and finally cracking that bottle of wine he was saving only to have it in a styrofoam cup at some fast food joint.

Some of the best acting I’ve ever seen; masterful.
[removed]
[removed]

Dwayne’s (Paul Dano) in Little Miss Sunshine breakdown, just because it’s so cathartic and the build up to it is so claustrophobically sad. Also, maybe not a “mental breakdown” but Emma Thompson trying to keep it together; physically swallowing back tears and fidgeting, and NOT breakdown for the sake of her children/family is incredibly performed.

Half the cast of Magnolia. Melora Walters; William H Macy; Jason Robards; Julianne Moore; Tom Cruise; the kid who plays Stanley. There are probably examples I am missing, William H Macy and Melora Walters are great, but the best for me is Jason Robards drugged up on morphine breakdown. He does a great job of selling it without being allowed to show strong emotion.

First one that comes to mind is Paul Dano in Little Miss Sunshine. From the dialogue to line delivery it’s all so perfect. I also really love Charlie’s in Perks of Being a Wallflower because it’s just so iconic and hits me deep every time
[removed]
[removed]
[removed]
[removed]
[removed]

Don't even know if I'd actually call it an emotional breakdown, but.. Rooney Mara's pie eating scene in A Ghost Story.

It's a pretty subtle and very divisive one. 

Just a girl, her pie, a ghost, and her grief.

I think the lack of the traditional big emotional acting is what makes it stick out for me.
[removed]
[removed]
Incidentally, I just watched this last night. Very emotional indeed.
Florence Pugh as Dani in Midsommar, when her boyfriend is walking up to her house and can hear her crying from outside. And then her screaming and sobbing while he holds her on the couch.
I had the same movie in mind but it's the end where she's screaming and sobbing during the ritual that sticks out in my mind more.
[removed]
Agreed. Always surprised that this film isn’t talked about more.

Children of Men, the scene after the ambush.  Avoiding spoilers, but if you've seen this you know the scene.

The way he just sort of numbly collects himself, performing like an automaton, and then when he's allowed a brief moment of peace, we see the real Theo, and his armor of numbness has failed him.  It hit me even harder because that is *exactly* how I reacted after a funeral for someone I was close to.  It was hard to watch someone else do that.
Also, Lee Guem ja stuffing her face into the Tofu cake at the end
[removed]

Maybe not a typical emotional breakdown, but that scene in *Hostiles* where Rory Cochrane tells Christian Bale that he has to move on is the most accurate depiction of PTSD leading to suicidal ideation that I've ever seen. Just calmly checked out. If you've been there it's like looking in a mirror.

"I can't feel anything." Fuck.

That scene in The Bad and the Beautiful is intense and one of the most memorable scenes like that in any movie. Did they use rear projection or something? It's a very creative way to use a visual to accent an emotion.

That scene took me out of the movie, because it made me think about Rooney Mara either starving herself a day to prepare for the scene, or forcing herself to barf after the director called "Cut!"  Or both.

In Leave No Trace, when the daughter recognizes and tells the father "What's wrong with you isn't what's wrong with me" and she decides to turn back and no longer follow him into isolation. It's an absolute breaking point of emotions for both characters, not in a super intense crying out loud way but in a really tragic letting go moment.
[removed]
[removed]
[removed]

Its not really film BUT that speech Barbara Stanwyck did in the Thorn Birds about her aging body and how young she still feels. It just such an acting moment. She sure does have her movie break down BUT this feels like a pinnacle. It felt real, her disgust, her want of the priest, and her pathetic-ness.  She is such a naturalistic actor.

Watched All of us strangers recently and the scene where the main character comes out to his father really got to me. It was maybe less intense than some others mentioned here, but felt very raw and real.
[removed]
No, I didn't see any rear projection and yes, it's a fantastic scene.
